name: production-linux-peer-bound multi-hour soak with scheduled retention
revision_note: Stricter only, before the final soak run: dedup probes resubmit recent completed request IDs (the earlier harness resubmitted the first ones, which a three-hour run has archived and Guard rightly refuses), and S-07 also requires that the earliest completed IDs, archived hours earlier, are refused as expired (10 per agent). No threshold was relaxed.
deployment: same topology and host as capacity-targets-production.json

targets.name: latency over the run and in every window, retention windows included
file descriptors and threads stay flat
retention runs on schedule during the run
integrity and no replay at the end
archive growth is proportional to traffic

measurement_rules: Archives are retained history and grow with traffic by design; S-08 bounds the rate. Active stores and process resources must plateau. A failed target is reported, not relaxed. Every agent must exit 0 and report its summary with at least 95 % of its offered requests; otherwise S-01 fails.

revisions.note: Revised before any soak measurement: the vault deletes expired entries inline on every insert, so the scheduled purge rarely finds any; the purge criterion now counts runs and S-05 bounds expired-but-present entries instead.

Stricter only, after an AI-assisted review of the harness and before the final run: S-01 also fails unless every agent exits 0 and reports at least 95 % of its offered requests. No threshold was relaxed.

Stricter only, before the final soak run: dedup probes resubmit recent completed request IDs (the earlier harness resubmitted the first ones, which a three-hour run has archived and Guard rightly refuses), and S-07 also requires that the earliest completed IDs, archived hours earlier, are refused as expired (10 per agent). No threshold was relaxed.
